title: Update on Singapore's Health Measures following Declaration of Mpox as Public Health Emergency of International Concern
what_it_is: Update on Singapore's Health Measures following Declaration of Mpox as Public Health Emergency of International Concern

sections.label: Parliamentary questions on mpox
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Health about mpox virus characteristics, border and social measures, vaccines, traveller screening, public awareness and risks to vulnerable residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health with monkeypox (mpox) declared by the World Health Organization as a public health emergency of international concern (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the characteristics of the virus and how it is evolving; (b) what are the border and social measures to deal with the situation; and (c) whether the Ministry has adequate mpox vaccines for our population.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the recent rise in monkeypox (mpox) cases in Africa (a) what protocols are in place for screening and monitoring travellers from regions with known mpox outbreaks, especially given the potential for cross-border transmission; and (b) what measures are being implemented to enhance public awareness of (i) mpox symptoms (ii) transmission modes and (iii) preventive practices in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the local mpox situation; (b) whether mpox poses a severe health risk to vulnerable residents such as seniors and children; and (c) whether there is a need for a nationwide rollout of mpox vaccines for these vulnerable residents.

sections.label: No mpox Clade I cases
sections.summary: As of 5 September 2024, Singapore has had no mpox Clade I cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of 5 September 2024, there have been no mpox Clade I cases in Singapore.

sections.label: Mpox Clade I reproduction number
sections.summary: The mpox Clade I virus has a known reproduction number, or R, of about 1.3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of now, the mpox Clade I virus has a known reproduction number, or "R", of about 1.3.

sections.label: Detect, isolate and quarantine approach
sections.summary: With an R of 1.3, the best way to suppress spread is to detect and isolate cases and quarantine close contacts early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With an R of 1.3 – and that is a decisive consideration – we think the best way to suppress the spread of the virus is to detect and isolate cases, and quarantine close contacts early to reduce the risk of spread to the community.

sections.label: Smallpox vaccine stock and vaccination stance
sections.summary: Smallpox vaccines called JYNNEOS are kept to counter orthopoxviruses, but population-wide mpox vaccination is not necessary or recommended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Although smallpox has been eradicated, we kept some stock of smallpox vaccines, called JYNNEOS, to counter orthopoxviruses, such as the mpox virus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Based on our current understanding of the disease and its relatively low reproduction rate, population-wide mpox vaccination is not necessary and not recommended.

sections.label: MOH assessment of mpox Clade I
sections.summary: MOH assesses that mpox Clade I is likely troublesome and inconvenient but manageable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MOH's bottomline assessment is that mpox Clade I is likely a troublesome virus which will cause us some inconvenience, but all in all, is something we can manage.

sections.label: Free mpox vaccine JYNNEOS
sections.summary: The mpox vaccine JYNNEOS will be offered free to healthcare workers directly exposed to the virus and as post-exposure prophylaxis for close contacts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, if they have not taken for some reason, it could be because it is not suitable for them, in which case, then I think we have to look at the other alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But I think, in general, the mpox vaccine JYNNEOS will be offered free to the two groups I mentioned – healthcare workers who are directly exposed to the virus in taking care of patients as well as post-exposure prophylaxis for close contacts of an infected person.

sections.label: Surveillance in camps, homes, dormitories
sections.summary: Closer surveillance will be implemented in settings such as camps, old folks' homes and foreign worker dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I understand from the Minister that there are already some measures in place for places such as preschools, but I want to know what about places such as camps where our Servicemen reside, old folks' homes where vulnerable seniors are situated and foreign worker dormitories as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think closer surveillance will be a good idea in those settings that the Member mentioned and they will be implemented.

sections.label: Public education and GP monitoring
sections.summary: The public should see a doctor when symptoms appear, and community monitoring is through GPs and family doctors briefed on protocols.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That relates to the second question, what is more important is to educate the general public that when you see such symptoms, please see a doctor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And then, the best community monitoring is still through our network of GPs and family doctors who have been briefed on what to look out for and what are the protocols.
